subject: Geomorphology, Afro-Alpine Microclimates, and Endemic Speciation in the Simien Massif

geographic_extent.peak_elevation: Ras Dejen (4,550m ASL - Fourth highest peak in Africa)
geographic_extent.cliff_vertical_drop: Up to 1,500m sheer vertical escarpments into the Tekeze River basin

geological_history.origin: Flood basalt volcanism during the Oligocene–Miocene epochs (approx. 30 million years ago)
geological_history.stratigraphy: Over 3,000 meters of piled basaltic lava traps and pyroclastic tuff known as the Ashangi and Shield Groups
geological_history.glacial_evidence: Cirques, U-shaped valleys, and moraine deposits from the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM c. 20,000 BP) above 3,600m

microclimatic_regimes.thermal_dynamics: Diurnal temperature fluctuations of 30°C: 'Summer every day, winter every night' (frost below 0°C nightly, warming to 20°C under equatorial sun)
microclimatic_regimes.precipitation: 1,400mm to 1,800mm annual bimodal rainfall driven by the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)

flora_adaptations.height: Up to 6 meters tall flowering spikes
flora_adaptations.thermal_insulation: Leaves fold into a tight nighttime rosette containing mucilaginous water reservoir that prevents freezing of apical meristem.

flora_adaptations.role: Forms elfin dwarf cloud forest belt along the 3,200m–3,800m tree-line zone.
